sections_target.text: Introduction

Steam power stations depend in their production of electrical energy on driving the turbines by the thrust of steam and its impact on the turbine blades, causing them to rotate at certain speeds. The steam used to drive the turbines is produced by equipment specially designed for this purpose called boilers, which are designed from materials that withstand high pressures and temperatures. Treated water (demineralized) is heated inside these boilers to convert it into steam. When it is necessary to shut down a boiler for operating or maintenance reasons, the boiler tubes must be protected from corrosion by what is known as the preservation process.

This document was prepared by Chemist Sherien Abdel Samei Eldakrory, revised by Chemist Mohamed Ramzy of the Chemical Department at the Steam Station (2 x 210 MW), reviewed by Chemist Mohamed Mosbah Mokpel, Chemistry Inspector in the Inspection and Quality Control Sector of East Delta Electricity Production Company, and approved by Eng. Awad Mohamed Fathy, Head Sector of Talkha Power Station.

This document is approved by Eng. Samir Abdel Galil Ahmed, General Director of Inspection and Quality Control and MPIS Coordinator at East Delta Electricity Production Company, and certified by Accountant Mahmoud Mohamed Soliman, General Director of Financial and Administrative Control and Supervisor of the Inspection and Quality Control Sector at East Delta Electricity Production Company.

sections_target.text: Procedures to be Carried Out
The different methods of preserving the boilers of the 210 MW unit according to the manufacturer instructions (8 methods).
Wet preservation method for the high- and medium-pressure groups of the boilers using a chemically treated aqueous solution.
Wet Preservation Method

rows: The boiler preservation process begins immediately after the boiler cools, as do the steam lines, so that the steam lines are at a temperature < 100°C.
The high- and medium-pressure lines of the boiler are isolated from the turbine.
In the steam pipe lines there are what are called isolation points, through which a blind flange can be installed if needed.
Feedwater is used with (50-100 mg/L) of hydrazine (N2H4) added to it.
The high-pressure parts (high-pressure systems) are filled through the filling line of the low-pressure parts of the boilers.
The medium-pressure parts (medium-pressure systems) are filled through the bypass of the high-pressure parts.
The hydrazine, the prepared chemical solution, is injected into the feedwater using the daily chemical injection equipment in the feedwater (injection pumps - daily treatment chemicals tank).
Samples are taken to determine the hydrazine content (content of Hydrazine) and the pH, through the blowdown points of the medium-pressure parts of the boilers, daily.

sections_target.text: Note: The boiler remains filled and chemically treated throughout the boiler shutdown period, noting that no air should leak into the preserved and chemically treated parts, with continued daily sampling to monitor (Content of Hydrazine & pH) and taking the necessary action if the specifications fall below the chemically permitted limits.
Wet preservation method for the high-pressure groups of the boilers using auxiliary steam.

Wet 
preservation
method for H-P
system 
of the Boiler with Auxiliary steam

rows: The drum is filled to the highest level.
The high-pressure parts are isolated according to the operating instruction steps.
When the pressure reaches (2-3) MPa, the high-pressure parts are connected to the distribution circuit of the operating auxiliary steam (1.2-1.5) MPa.
The pressure in the boiler quickly falls below the auxiliary steam pressure, and steam begins to enter the superheaters, which gradually fill.
Final state: (the economizer, evaporators and drum) are filled with feedwater, and the superheaters are under auxiliary steam pressure.
Note: Feedwater is used with (50-100 mg/L) of hydrazine (N2H4) added to it.
The water is tested daily to measure (content of hydrazine) and the pH.
Samples are taken through a sampling pipe at the outlet of the high-pressure parts.

When the hydrazine content falls and the pH value is low, the condensate is blown down through the blowdown points of the superheaters, and the superheaters are refilled and pressurized with auxiliary steam.
Note: The quality of the auxiliary steam must be sufficient and in accordance with the operating instruction steps.

sections_target.text: Wet preservation method for the high-pressure group of the boilers under nitrogen pressure.

Wet Method of the High Pressure 
System of the Boiler with Nitrogen

rows: Immediately after the boiler stops, the drum must be filled at maximum speed to the highest level.
When the boiler pressure falls to (0.5 MPa), the nitrogen cylinder is connected to the superheater vents.

The cylinder pressure is regulated to suit the height of the water column in the boiler, so that all the high-pressure parts filled with feedwater and steam condensate or nitrogen are under high pressure.
All boiler pressure fittings must be closed.
As the boiler cools, the pressure gradually falls inside the boiler and soon the pressure inside the boiler reaches the operating pressure of the cylinder pressure-reducing valve.
Nitrogen automatically begins to enter the superheaters, and the cylinder is replaced with another filled one.
Final state
The high-pressure parts of the boilers, the economizer, evaporators and drum are filled with feedwater.
The steam superheaters are filled with steam condensate and nitrogen.
During the boiler preservation process, periodic tests are carried out so that the pressure of the boiler as a whole is always less than (0.03 MPa).
If nitrogen consumption tends to increase, the person monitoring the boiler must test all closed vents, drain points and samples to locate the leak and prevent it from the high-pressure parts.

After the boiler cools, the volume of water in the boiler will decrease, so the volume of the pressurized part preserved with nitrogen may decrease; therefore the boiler is filled with feedwater to the highest level in the drum.
About one hour before shutting down the boiler, the (hydrazine content) in the pressurized parts filled with feedwater must comply with the preservation instructions.
A sample is taken every two weeks to measure the hydrazine content and the pH.

sections_target.text: Dry preservation method for the high- and medium-pressure groups of the boilers with air.
Dry Preservation Method of the H-P & M-P Systems of Boiler with Air

rows: After shutting down the boiler at a pressure of (0.2 MPa) in the high-pressure parts and (0.5 MPa) in the medium-pressure parts, the blowdown is opened.
After the venting process is completed, the boiler is closed on air and part of the flue gases.
After the draining and evaporation process through blowdown, all high- and medium-pressure parts are drained with the aid of vacuum in the condenser.
After completing the draining process, dry air preservation begins through the ventilation groups for the high- and medium-pressure parts of the boilers.
The relative humidity of the air must be tested periodically from sampling points designed for this purpose, and the relative humidity must be less than 50%.
During the preservation period, periodic tests must be carried out so that all high- and medium-pressure parts always maintain an excess pressure of at least (0.3 Pa).
The volume of air required for the preservation process is approximately (600 m³/hour).

sections_target.text: Dry preservation of the medium-pressure parts of the boilers.

Dry Preservation Method for 
Medium 
Pressure System of the Boiler

rows: After the boiler stops, the medium-pressure parts are drained while still hot, then drained by the condenser (Vacuumized into the condenser).
The draining process is carried out immediately after stopping combustion to ensure evaporation and initial drying in the parts where steam is reheated (Reheaters).
Immediately after evaporation and initial drying, dry air preservation is carried out by the ventilation groups of the (Reheaters).
During the preservation time, pressure and humidity tests are carried out in the (Reheaters) and the combustion chamber.

sections_target.text: Preservation with nitrogen after repair or inspection operations in the high-pressure parts of the boilers.

Preservation with Nitrogen 
after Repairs or Inspecting Operations in the H-P System of the Boiler

rows: The boiler is fired according to the operating steps and instructions from the cold state.
After the pressure reaches (0.5 MPa) in the boiler, the (burners) are stopped and the nitrogen cylinder is connected to the superheater vents.

The cylinder pressure is regulated to suit the height of the water column in the boiler, so that all the high-pressure parts filled with feedwater and steam condensate or nitrogen are under high pressure.
All boiler pressure fittings must be closed.
As the boiler cools, the pressure gradually falls inside the boiler and soon the pressure inside the boiler reaches the operating pressure of the cylinder pressure-reducing valve.
Nitrogen automatically begins to enter the superheaters.
When the cylinder is emptied by all the nitrogen entering the superheaters, it is replaced with another filled cylinder.
When the pressure in the superheaters falls to (zero MPa), all vents, drains, steam sampling points, water blowdown points and reheated steam sampling points are closed (they must be closed).
The pressurized part must be drained for two hours.
To complete the draining process, the boiler and steam lines are left to cool.

sections_target.text: Note: During assembly and installation operations, all places through which air can penetrate into the boiler must be closed, and if the boiler is not put into operation after completing the repair operations, the air must be removed from the boiler and it must be preserved; therefore the boiler manufacturer recommends under these conditions preserving the boiler using nitrogen.
Method of preserving the boilers by keeping the boiler pressure continuously high.

Preservation of the Boiler 
by over Pressure being Maintained in it
Note: This method is for a boiler shutdown of less than one week.

rows: In the case of a planned shutdown, or according to the instructions of the responsible person, for less than one week, it is recommended to preserve the boiler by keeping the pressure inside it above (0.1 MPa).
This preservation method enables us to preserve the medium-pressure parts under a pressure slightly lower than that of the high-pressure parts, by opening the reducing station half open on average.
The excess pressure in the boiler is above (0.1 MPa) and is obtained by temporary heating with (1) or (2) burners, following all operating instructions.
The boiler must be completely isolated from the turbine, so we do not need to add heat during the preservation process except after long periods.
After the boiler stops, according to the amount of heat contained in it, the pressure in the closed pressurized parts rises, so the pressure may reach the maximum permitted value.
Control must be exercised by the reducing stations of the high- and medium-pressure parts by opening them half open for a short time at intervals.

The boiler shutdown will be affected accordingly with the operating instructions corresponding to the boiler shutdown specifications, so the preservation process can begin by means of the excess pressure mentioned.

sections_target.text: Dry preservation of the boilers with the aid of condenser vacuum and the accumulated (latent) heat in the boilers and steam lines.

Dry Preservation of 
the Boiler with the Help of Vacuum in the Condenser and the Heat Accumulated in 
the Boiler Steam Pipe Lines
Note:

rows: The basis of this method is that the internal surface of the pressurized parts dries completely using the latent (accumulated) heat in the insulation - the brickwork of the boilers - and the boiler material itself.
A
The water is blown down from the boiler and the steam, then it is disposed of from the pressurized parts with the aid of the turbine vacuum equipment.
B
The advantage of this method is that the pressurized parts can work well after completing the preservation process, so no additions of new equipment are needed if this method is used.
C

When preserving by this method, the quality of preservation is lower compared to other methods, since interference in the pressurized parts is possible at the same time, and thus atmospheric air can leak into the preserved parts.
D

sections_target.text: Preservation steps

rows: Combustion is shut down (Combustion Shut-Down) at the following specifications: boiler output (out put of the boiler) (50%). Superheater steam pressure (Pressure of superheater steam) (6.8) MPa. Superheater steam temperature (Heat of superheater steam) (500-520°C). Reheated steam temperature (Top-of reheated steam) (500-520°C).
Stopping the individual equipment is carried out according to the boiler operating instructions.
The pressure drop in the boiler must be controlled by the high- and low-pressure bypasses at a rate of (0.1 MPa), and boiler blowdown is started immediately.
Blowdown of the feed lines, economizer and evaporators is opened, but the sudden drop in boiler pressure may not cause an increase in the maximum permitted pressure in the drum.
At a pressure of about (0.5 MPa) for the superheated steam, all blowdowns of the superheaters, the Reheaters and the steam lines must be opened.
At a pressure of about (0.2 MPa) for the superheated steam, all vents and air outlet valves of the boilers and steam lines are opened.
